checks: Checked a21ff89aef880b49 opening (1)–(3) and §3, (10) against the pinned archive and declared SHA. The source proves the weak implication; the draft also proves the valid strict variant by separately retaining the strict gap at the appropriate end of the comparison.

The domain is compact and nonempty for every d≥1. Coupling all exponentials in a fixed dimension gives almost-sure convergence of the sums, and −E₀ gives no atom at zero. Zero padding preserves the same fixed coefficient, balance, bounds and sign probability, so the attained c_d are nonincreasing.

A weak counterexample supplies c_d ≤ c_{d₀}<c thereafter; a strict counterexample supplies c_d≤c. The all-unit-negative branch gives ≥1/2>c in either case. For all-unit-positive lists, the residual negative total is k−1; the p=0 specialization gives ≥G_{k,0}, with the exact value 1/2 if k=1.

The fractional classification excludes zeros at every minimizing vector in that branch; hence k_d+m_d=d−1 uses the original dimension, including when the dimension ladder is formed by zero padding. Padding a vector does not claim that it remains a minimizer.

Unbounded k_d gives a subsequence with k_d→∞ even when m_d grows at the same time, and the uniform limit 1/2 contradicts c_d≤c<1/2. Otherwise take a constant k subsequence, then p_d→p in [0,1]; the count identity forces m_d→∞ along it and the limit is G_{k,p}.

The weak contradiction compares the uniform strict upper bound c_{d₀}<c to G_{k,p}≥c. The strict contradiction compares the weak upper bound c_d≤c to G_{k,p}>c. No uniform strict surplus or attainment of an infimum across dimensions is used.
